old: In spoken Hungarian, speakers often colloquially say 'aminek a területén'. In elevated B2 essays and architectural evaluations, always write 'amelynek területén' or 'amelynek mentén', omitting the definite article after amelynek for elegant conciseness.
new: In spoken Hungarian, speakers often say 'aminek a területén'. 'Amelynek a területén' is equally correct; in elevated B2 essays and architectural evaluations the article after amelynek is often dropped for conciseness: 'amelynek területén', 'amelynek szélén'.
why: "always ... omitting the article" is wrong: both forms are correct (so fill-blanks take both)

old: révén governs the genitive/nominative -> amelynek révén = 'by means of which'.
new: révén takes either the bare noun or the possessor form in -nak/-nek (valaminek a révén), so amely révén, amelynek révén and amelynek a révén are all correct = 'by means of which'.
why: "governs the genitive/nominative" is a wrong description; and a fill-blank on amelynek révén has three equal answers
